feature_overview.business_goal: Deliver the Item Notes feature for the E-commerce application.
scope: Allow registered users to add a short text note to a catalog item.
Display all notes for a catalog item, sorted by creation date (newest first).
out_of_scope: Notes on items not accessible to the user.
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Item Notes feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: Users can add a short text note to a catalog item and view every note left on that item, newest first.

acceptance_criteria.description: A user can successfully submit a note for an item and see it appear in the list.
Notes are displayed in descending order of creation date.
The system prevents submission of notes exceeding 500 characters.

validation_rules.description: Note content must not exceed 500 characters.
Only registered users can submit notes.

non_functional_requirements.description: The system shall support up to 100 notes per item.
The system shall ensure that note content is sanitized to prevent XSS attacks.

architecture_approach.architecture_rationale: Use modular to keep the Item Notes feature separated into presentation, business logic, and data responsibilities where applicable.
architecture_approach.frontend_overview: Frontend design should provide the user-facing entry points, inputs, states, and feedback required by the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.backend_overview: Backend design should process feature requests, enforce business rules, validate inputs, and return structured responses.
architecture_approach.data_overview: Data design should support the data requirements defined in the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.integration_overview: Integration design should follow the API expectations and dependencies listed in the approved SRS.
design_tradeoffs: Design is derived directly from the approved SRS to preserve traceability and feature scope.
Design is kept feature-scoped to preserve feature-by-feature SDLC development.
Internal generation or repair details are kept in backend logs and are not exposed in the approval-ready Architecture Plan.

implementation_order: Create the Mongoose model(s): models/ItemNotesDataEntity1.ts, models/ItemNotesDataEntity2.ts, models/ItemNotesDataEntity3.ts, models/ItemNotesDataEntity4.ts

Create app/api/item-notes/route.ts implementing /api/item-notes, /api/item-notes, validating required request fields before use (400 on missing/malformed) -- it is automatically live the instant the file exists, no separate mount step needed.
Create lib/api/itemNotes.ts with one function per endpoint.
Create app/item-notes/page.tsx (a Client Component, `"use client"` as its first line), reusing approved UI/UX components where available instead of re-authoring their markup.
Register a real <Link href="/item-notes"> in app/page.tsx at the FEATURE_LINKS markers -- a page with no link to it is not complete.
constraints: The Next.js App Router scaffold already exists and works -- never recreate app/layout.tsx, next.config.mjs, tsconfig.json, or lib/mongodb.ts.
A Route Handler (route.ts) is live the instant it exists -- there is no router to mount it on, unlike an Express app.js.
Register new pages by adding a real <Link href="..."> in app/page.tsx (FEATURE_LINKS markers) -- an unreachable page is not done.
Every Mongoose model file must use the `mongoose.models.X || mongoose.model(...)` guard to avoid OverwriteModelError.
Reuse approved UI/UX components verbatim (via read_ui_component) instead of re-authoring their markup.
